newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
--Following the negative response to a proposal to reduce working hours and pay, the government is now expected to propose more flexible working hours within the 40-hour framework.
--Sales of Treasury bills and zero coupon bonds in February raised 795 billion drachmas for the state, overshooting targets by 211 billion.
--There are concerns about the rate for revenues collected for the state, with incoming tax revenues last month at 6.5 percent, well below the forecast target of 14.6 percent.

--The Athens bourse is stabilising after the buffeting it received last week. Yesterday's session ended with the general price index up 0.54 percent, following coordinated action by state-run banks and other state portfolios.

--Business is now facing completing a different complicated tax form - the form on real estate and property owned by firms, which will form the basis for the real estate tax. The form is different to the 'E9', which must be submitted by all individuals along with income declarations.
--The second Greek telecoms organisation OTE share offer will be offered in two stages: an initial offer of 10 percent and, in line with the market conditions, an increased percentage.
--The finance ministry has begun checks on all electronic cash registers in an effort to detect non-authorised transactions that result in failure to pay VAT.

--The national economy and development ministries are making the final efforts to sell off ailing state-run firms, using the 5.5 billion drachma line item in the state budget to retrench workers at the Elefsina Shipyards.

--Each ministry has essentially received a six-month deadline for the greatest possible absorption of Community funds, pending the meeting in the autumn of a European Union Monitoring Committee which will be empowered to transfer unused funds.
--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou told Parliament yesterday that February inflation had fallen to 6.5 percent from 6.8 in January.
--Despite developments on the stock exchange, banks are determined to proceed with planned share capital increases.

--Greek firms active in Albania yesterday called on the government for help and the creation of a special insurance fund for compensation and damages, stressing that they were the first to respond to the government's call to invest Albania. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
